applies_when: The structured diagnostic comes from xvlog 2026.1 with error code VRFC 10-1280.
The object is actually assigned in a procedural block such as always, and its declaration and language mode are visible.
not_applicable_when: The assignment is continuous (such as assign), or the diagnostic comes from another tool or an unknown version.
The object is driven only by assign statements or instance ports.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Interpret the error as an incompatibility between the declaration and procedural driving, then look for the corresponding repair method; do not replace declarations in bulk.

When the public task imposes no additional type restriction, a procedurally assigned output in Verilog may be declared output reg in its ANSI port declaration; SystemVerilog may use an appropriate variable type such as logic.
Preserve port names, directions, and widths, and check for other drivers.
verification: Re-run the same xvlog stage, confirm the error code disappears, and check for newly exposed multiple drivers.
Check the interface and re-run xvlog and xelab; after compilation and elaboration pass, continue with independent functional checks.
hard_negatives: A wire driven by a continuous assignment does not need to become a reg.
Do not mechanically replace every wire with reg or logic.
cards.title: Check variable declarations for procedural assignment targets

applies_when: The module header uses ANSI port declarations and xvlog reports a corresponding port redeclaration.
The module header contains directions and types and therefore uses ANSI declarations.
not_applicable_when: The module uses a non-ANSI port list, or identical names belong to distinct valid scopes.
The module header lists only port names and therefore uses non-ANSI style.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Confirm the port declaration style before applying the ANSI-port repair method.
Complete the direction, type, and width declaration in the module header and remove the duplicate declaration from the body.
verification: Parse the module header and body declarations, then re-run xvlog.
Check the port set, directions, and widths, then run xvlog.
hard_negatives: Non-ANSI style requires directions and types to be declared in the module body.
Do not delete body declarations required by non-ANSI style.
cards.title: Declare ANSI ports exactly once in the module header

applies_when: xvlog reports a syntax error or a keyword in an invalid context during parsing.
The parser reports the first syntax error and the surrounding source can be read.
not_applicable_when: The code already parses successfully and fails only functional verification.
The code has passed parsing and has only functional or timing issues.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Treat the reported location as a starting point; also inspect the preceding statement and surrounding begin/end blocks.
Check the current and preceding statements, parentheses, semicolons, begin/end blocks, and module-header terminators.
verification: Parse again after the repair and use the new first error as the reference.
Parse again and identify the first error anew; do not merely confirm that the original line no longer reports an error.
hard_negatives: Do not unconditionally append a semicolon at the reported line whenever syntax error appears.
The reported line may merely be a victim of a preceding unclosed statement.
cards.title: Inspect local context backward from the first syntax error

applies_when: xvlog explicitly reports that an identifier is undeclared in the current scope.
The diagnostic name and its use site are visible.
not_applicable_when: The identifier is declared but its width, direction, or functionality is wrong.
The name is correctly declared but its type or width is incompatible.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Distinguish misspelling, a missing declaration, a scope error, and macro-expansion issues.
Check spelling, declarations, scope, and preprocessing conditions in order; use the public interface as the authority for port names.
verification: Re-run parsing after the repair and verify that interface names were not changed without authorization.
Re-run xvlog and check that no implicit net or interface drift was introduced.
hard_negatives: Do not automatically add an implicit wire for an unknown name merely to suppress the error.
Creating a new signal with the reported name can hide a spelling error.
cards.title: Four checks for an undeclared identifier

applies_when: The diagnostic explicitly identifies a non-printable character or byte value.
The tool reports the location or value of an anomalous byte.
not_applicable_when: There is an ordinary Verilog syntax error without character-encoding evidence.
There is only a general syntax error with no character evidence.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Locate the anomalous byte and replace only unintentionally introduced characters while preserving RTL semantics.
Use a byte-level view to locate and replace anomalous characters without changing valid identifiers or RTL structure.
verification: Check the file encoding and re-run xvlog.
Confirm the file encoding is stable and run parsing again.
hard_negatives: Do not remove non-ASCII text in valid comments or strings without evidence.
Chinese comments do not, by themselves, imply invalid source bytes.
cards.title: Remove only source-byte anomalies supported by evidence

applies_when: Vivado synth_design 2026.1 reports multiple drivers on an object.
The synthesis diagnostic can bind two or more drivers to the same object.
not_applicable_when: There are only multiple readers, or the tool has not identified multiple drivers.
Multiple conditional branches are in one procedural block, or multiple logic blocks only read the same object.
Do not use a general repair suggestion that conflicts with explicit type, interface, or behavioral constraints in the public task.
guidance: Enumerate every driver formed by continuous assignments, procedural blocks, and instance outputs.
List every procedural block, continuous assignment, and instance output, retaining a single-driver structure consistent with the specification.
verification: Synthesize again after merging or removing incorrect drivers and run functional regression checks.
Synthesize again and functionally verify overlapping control conditions and default paths.
hard_negatives: Multiplexer logic is not equivalent to multiple concurrent drivers; do not arbitrarily delete a functional branch.
Do not delete the first or last driver merely because of its position in the log.
cards.title: Enumerate and consolidate multiple drivers by object
